proposed_changes.note: Revised against the Greek and expanded edition combining the 1882 and 1890 volumes, with the offices of the liturgical day, the Great Canon, dismissals, Sunday propers, calendar and a paschalion for 1921–1960. Its preface states that the canonical parts of the liturgies were printed in Greek as well, so that clergy could celebrate the essential part in the Church's original language until Greek liturgikons could be obtained from Rome (Athanasiana 27 (2008), printed p. 20, quoting the book's 'Emlékezetül', pp. 309–310). Distribution was announced by circular 1195 and the text made binding by circular 1021 of 1921. Open: do not date all public use from the private-use permission alone; book not acquired. Follow-up 2026-10-20: Ivancsó 2007, pp. 69–73, and Ivancsó 2008, pp. 19–25, re-inspected. The approval formula is permission for private use and must remain explicit. Dated circular 1021/1921 directs the revised book’s wording; circular 2351/1949 describes the heavily worn Chrysostom section of 1920 copies and orders a replacement extract. This documents operative local reception without establishing papal approval, public-use permission from 1920 alone, first celebration or universal compliance. The 1984 printing is reported as an unchanged reprint, not a new recension. Batch 3 follow-up (2026-10-20): all four offered photographs of seller item 32188629463 inspected. The unnumbered title leaf directly controls the reproduced 1920 title, private-use formula 1235/1920, revised/expanded statement and Jóba Elek printer line 1723–1920, but original-impression authentication is unresolved because the 1984 facsimile retains that imprint. Whole contents, dated approval verso and Emlékezetül remain unacquired. College record bibNY56K501 supplies exact separate copies Ant10911/M-1638, Ant10792/M-1637 (missing pp. 273–311, with catalogued August 1920 preparatory annotations), and Ant101011/M-1891 (Hajdúböszörmény parish stamps); annotations and stamps were not seen. No first-use or public-altar-use claim follows.
